text:
**Short answer:** A power station of about 1,000 Wh is enough for one night. I'd pick the **BLUETTI Elite 100 V2** (1,024 Wh), or the **EcoFlow Delta 3 Classic** (1,024 Wh) if you want a bigger, more heavily backed unit.

**Why 1,000 Wh works**
- Electric blankets use little power. The Department of Energy figures cited by [Tested Watts](https://testedwatts.com/2026/09/24/power-station-electric-blanket/) are about 60 W for a single and 100 W for a double. Sunbeam rates its full-size blankets at 110 W. At 100 W, a 1,024 Wh unit runs about 8 hours, roughly one night.
- [Blackout Wise](https://www.blackoutwise.com/will-it-run/electric-blanket) says a queen blanket is rated about 150 W but cycles to an average of about 75 W. On that basis a 1,000 Wh unit runs it for 11 to 12 hours.
- One source is more conservative. [Home Power Facts](https://homepowerfacts.com/can-it-run/electric-blanket/) assumes a 260 W average draw for a queen blanket. It says you'd need about 2,600 Wh for 8 hours. That is much higher than the other sources, and a blanket on a low setting will use less. If you run a queen blanket on high all night, size up.

**My picks**
1. **BLUETTI Elite 100 V2** is the top pick in [Blackout Wise's guide](https://www.blackoutwise.com/best/best-power-station-for-electric-blanket). Its 1,024 Wh battery runs a 150 W blanket for about 12 hours. It usually sells for roughly $380 to $500 and weighs 25 lb. For two nights, they suggest the Jackery Explorer 2000 v2, at about 23 hours.
2. **EcoFlow Delta 3 Classic** has a 1,024 Wh LFP battery, 1,800 W AC output, and a five-year warranty. The [TechRadar](https://www.techradar.com/pro/this-ecoflow-delta-3-classic-bundle-is-the-home-backup-battery-id-keep-ready-for-winter-storms-and-its-usd119-off-at-best-buy) deal bundles it with a 45W solar panel for $479 (was $598) at Best Buy. TechRadar hasn't tested this model itself. It also notes that the 45W panel is too small to recharge the battery quickly, and the unit is 26.7 lb.
3. **BLUETTI AC180** (1,152 Wh, 1,800 W) is listed by [Dealectric](https://dealectric.com/power-station-to-run-a-heated-blanket-all-night) at $449. They say it runs one 120 V blanket all night, or two on low. It draws about 15 W itself with AC on. Dealectric says it's due back in stock in late November, so check availability. [Buy link](https://dealectric.com/go/bluetti-ac180).

**What to avoid**
- Units around 300 Wh are too small. [Blackout Wise](https://www.blackoutwise.com/best/best-power-station-for-electric-blanket) says a 286 to 288 Wh unit runs a 150 W blanket for only about 3 to 3.5 hours. The 499 Wh Yeti 500 reaches about 5.5 hours.
- The Tenergy T320 has a 200 W inverter. Dealectric says it can't run a 120 V queen blanket on high.

**Tips**
- Plug the blanket straight into the station. Sunbeam's manuals say not to use extension cords or power strips, per [Dealectric](https://dealectric.com/power-station-to-run-a-heated-blanket-all-night).
- Keep the station off the bed and away from the blanket's folds.
- If you also use a CPAP, [Blackout Wise](https://www.blackoutwise.com/will-it-run/electric-blanket) says the two together average about 109 W. A 1,000 Wh unit lasts about 8 hours in that case.

Tell me your blanket's wattage (it's on the tag) and whether you need it for more than one night. I can then narrow this down.
